subject: [Escalation] p95 surge on m13-epsilon — rollback authorization requested

Cc: ops@starlend.com
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: urgent: checkout latency spike (m13-epsilon) impacting transactions

Hi Tessa,

We're seeing a sudden p95 jump on calls routed to model m13-epsilon over the last 45 minutes — latency is up ~350ms at p95 and our checkout errors are climbing. This started after the midnight push you ran and coincides with higher concurrency from our EU batch jobs.

Can you confirm whether this is expected? Our customers are seeing slow checkout and some sessions are timing out. We need an ETA for mitigation or a temporary backout to the previous model if that's available.

Logs attached (ops@ attached a brief summary).

Thanks,
Lina

On Wed, Nov 3, 2027 at 09:24 AM Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Forwarding Lina's alert — this is landing in production as a p95 latency spike tied to m13-epsilon.

We dug into the serving metrics and KV cache hit-rate dropped significantly for the new quantization path on m13-epsilon when sequence lengths exceeded ~512 tokens. The kernel fallback increases per-token CPU on the host and amplifies queuing at 95th percentile. Detailed notes:

- Symptom: p95 increased from ~120ms -> ~470ms over 30-45m
- Trigger: unusual traffic mix (EU batch jobs + interactive sessions) caused longer sequences and lower cache reuse
- Immediate mitigation options:
  * A: Canary rollback: shift 40% traffic to m12-stable for 30m, observe p95. If stable, shift remaining 60% over 20m.
  * B: Traffic split to variant with disabled quant path (temp) — needs infra toggle, ~15m to enable.
  * C: Full rollback to m12-stable — fastest to restore but requires approval for prod change.

We have two artifacts attached: p95-trend-20271103.csv and m13-epsilon-kvcache-stats.txt. Connor will run a preflight (canary plan) and I can implement the rollout if we get approval. Note: rolling back will change model variant IDs in routing; dependents using pinned versions must be handled (we have a small set of pinned customers but Starlend was on auto-route).

Recommend option A (staged traffic split). For A we need authorization from Marissa for an exception to the rollout guard and Ben to confirm customer comms/credits.

-Markus
Staff SW Eng, Serving Runtime

Attachment: p95-trend-20271103.csv (csv)
Attachment: m13-epsilon-kvcache-stats.txt (text)
